35991581.clinical_problem: detecting intussusception on abdominal ultrasound in children
35991581.patient_population: 440 cases (373 pediatric intussusception, 67 normal) retrospectively collected from a children's hospital
35991581.model_description: An improved Faster R-CNN object detector takes abdominal ultrasound images as input and outputs detection/classification of the 'concentric circle' sign used to diagnose intussusception.
35991581.headline_result: Detection: 92.8% detection rate, 95.0% recall, 92.2% specificity, F1 86.4%; classification accuracy 93.0% on validation set
35991581.study_design: retrospective single-center model development with internal validation

36047281.body_region: craniofacial, shoulder and pelvic growth centers
36047281.clinical_problem: delineating skeletal growth centers to avoid radiation-induced growth abnormalities during childhood cancer radiotherapy planning
36047281.patient_population: 107 childhood cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy planning (training n=80, test n=27)
36047281.model_description: A modified U-Net with triplet-attention branches takes axial/coronal/sagittal CT slices as input and outputs auto-segmented contours of 19 skeletal growth-center structures.
36047281.headline_result: Average Dice 0.77-0.87 across groups; auto-contouring cut manual correction time by 72% (37.6 min saved of 52.2 min)
36047281.study_design: retrospective model development with internal test-cohort validation

36068030.clinical_problem: measuring axial vertebral rotation on radiographs to assess scoliosis progression risk
36068030.patient_population: 221 vertebrae from 17 spinal radiographs of adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis
36068030.model_description: CNN-based segmentation (spinal column, individual vertebra, pedicles) on posteroanterior radiographs is used to automatically calculate axial vertebral rotation, compared with manual measurement.
36068030.headline_result: 81% of automatic measurements within clinical acceptance error (±5°); mean absolute difference 4.3° ± 5.7° vs. manual
36068030.study_design: retrospective method-development study comparing automatic vs. manual measurement

36090673.clinical_problem: distinguishing bipolar disorder from major depressive disorder in adolescents
36090673.patient_population: 309 adolescents from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study (116 bipolar disorder, 64 major depressive disorder, 129 healthy)
36090673.model_description: A multimodal support vector machine takes resting-state functional connectivity plus structural MRI measures (cortical thickness, area, volume, sulcal depth) as input and classifies adolescents into diagnostic groups (bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, healthy).
36090673.headline_result: Multimodal classifier: 98.5% MDD vs. bipolar; leave-one-site-out accuracy 63.3-81.7%
36090673.study_design: retrospective multi-site classifier development with leave-one-site-out validation

36113502.exclusion_reason: clinical decision-tree model using only clinical and laboratory parameters, explicitly without imaging, for pediatric appendicitis diagnosis

36207092.clinical_problem: segmenting multiple bones on pediatric musculoskeletal MRI for morphological/diagnostic evaluation
36207092.patient_population: pediatric ankle and shoulder MRI datasets, pathological and healthy examinations
36207092.model_description: A pre-trained convolutional encoder-decoder segmentation network, regularized with shape priors from an auto-encoder and an adversarial discriminator, takes pediatric MR images as input and outputs multi-bone segmentation masks.
36207092.dataset_size: not stated (two scarce pediatric imaging datasets from ankle and shoulder joints)
36207092.headline_result: Outperformed or matched prior approaches on Dice, sensitivity, specificity and surface-distance metrics (exact values not given in abstract)

36238349.exclusion_reason: EEG-based pain classification; non-imaging physiological signal, not radiology

36348326.clinical_problem: bone age assessment in preschool children and its effect on reader agreement
36348326.patient_population: 56 bone age radiographs of preschool children (3-6 years) read by 6 residents
36348326.model_description: AI-assisted bone age software estimates skeletal maturity from hand-wrist radiographs (TW3-RUS and TW3-Carpal) to assist resident readers, compared against expert-consensus reference bone age.
36348326.release_evidence: AI-assisted diagnosis software for bone age described as a deployed clinical tool
36348326.headline_result: AI assistance improved inter- and intra-observer ICC agreement and reduced RMSE/MAD vs. no AI assistance

36680923.clinical_problem: discriminating developmental dyslexia, developmental coordination disorder, and their comorbidity in children using brain imaging
36680923.patient_population: 136 children (42 typically developing, 45 dyslexia, 20 coordination disorder, 29 comorbid)
36680923.model_description: Machine learning models are trained on structural (grey/white matter volume) and resting-state functional MRI indices (activity, local/global connectivity) to discriminate between developmental dyslexia, developmental coordination disorder, and comorbid children.
36680923.headline_result: No single imaging index discriminated groups alone; combined structural or functional models could discriminate among groups (no single accuracy figure given)

37614415.clinical_problem: improving downstream segmentation of longitudinal brain MRI, including developing infant brain MRI, by better pretraining
37614415.patient_population: longitudinal neurodegenerative adult MRI and developing infant brain MRI cohorts (sizes not stated)
37614415.model_description: A local, multi-scale spatiotemporal self-supervised pretraining method for image-to-image architectures takes longitudinal MRI scans as input and learns representations later fine-tuned for segmentation tasks with a self-supervised consistency regularization.
37614415.headline_result: Outperformed randomly-initialized baselines and existing self-supervised techniques on segmentation benchmarks (no single number reported in abstract)
37614415.study_design: retrospective method-development study benchmarked across segmentation tasks

33436974.clinical_problem: measuring ventricular volume in preterm infants with post-hemorrhagic ventricular dilatation
33436974.patient_population: 152 serial 3D ultrasound scans from 10 preterm infants with post-hemorrhagic ventricular dilatation (mean birth weight 1233 g, mean GA 28.1 weeks)
33436974.model_description: A 2D convolutional neural network takes 3D cranial ultrasound volumes as input and outputs automatic segmentation of brain ventricles, from which ventricular volume is calculated.
33436974.dataset_size: 152 3D ultrasound scans from 10 preterm infants; 230 manually segmented ventricles (108 training, 122 validation)

33560889.clinical_problem: assessing bone age in children living at high altitude (Tibet) using an AI system developed on a different population
33560889.model_description: A previously reported fully-automated AI bone-age system, trained on Han Chinese children from southern China, takes left-hand radiographs as input and outputs an estimated Greulich-Pyle bone age, compared with expert consensus reads.
33560889.headline_result: Accuracy within 1 year: 84.67% (Tibetan), 89.41% (Han); MAD 0.65 and 0.56 years respectively
33560889.study_design: retrospective external-population validation of an existing AI bone-age system

33637807.clinical_problem: differentiating pediatric high-grade brain tumor histology (tumor cellularity, necrosis, hemorrhage) noninvasively
33637807.patient_population: pediatric patients with high-grade brain tumors (sample size not stated in abstract)
33637807.model_description: A deep neural network takes diffusion basis spectrum imaging (DBSI)-derived diffusion metrics as input classifiers and outputs classification of tumor histology components (normal white matter, dense/less-dense tumor, infiltrating edge, necrosis, hemorrhage).
33637807.headline_result: Overall classification accuracy 85.8%; AUC 0.950-0.991 across tumor histology classes

33728035.clinical_problem: diagnosing pneumonia (and distinguishing bacterial from viral) in children from chest radiographs
33728035.patient_population: a widely used (relabeled) pediatric chest radiograph dataset
33728035.model_description: Statistical and deep-learning-derived global features are extracted from chest radiographs and combined for classification by a RandomForest classifier, outputting a three-class label (normal, bacterial pneumonia, viral pneumonia).
33728035.dataset_size: not stated (widely used relabeled chest radiograph dataset)
33728035.study_design: retrospective model-development study on a public dataset

33966055.clinical_problem: predicting 2-year neurodevelopmental outcome after neonatal encephalopathy from early diffusion MRI
33966055.patient_population: 15 term newborns with neonatal encephalopathy (5 normal, 5 abnormal motor outcome, 5 death)
33966055.model_description: A random forest classifier takes diffusion-weighted imaging connectome and fixel-based analysis metrics from MRI obtained in the first 4 weeks of life as input and predicts 2-year motor outcome category (normal, abnormal motor, death).

34007875.exclusion_reason: prediction model built mainly from fetal/maternal ECG-derived signal features (with standard Doppler/biometry), a clinical-variable/signal-based prediction model rather than image-based radiology AI

34063695.exclusion_reason: optical coherence tomography (OCT) of the middle ear; non-radiologic imaging modality excluded per protocol

34209154.clinical_problem: segmenting the fetus on MRI to aid diagnosis and clinical decision-making
34209154.model_description: Cross Attention Squeeze Excitation Network (CASE-Net) takes 2D fetal MR images as input and outputs whole-body fetal segmentation masks, combining attention mechanisms with squeeze-and-excitation blocks.
34209154.headline_result: Dice score 87.36%, outperforming competing segmentation architectures

34319165.clinical_problem: whether FDA-cleared AI tools for medical imaging triage/detection/diagnosis are adequately developed and validated for use in children
34319165.patient_population: children broadly, as a population underrepresented in FDA-cleared AI imaging tools
34319165.model_description: A perspective/commentary reviewing the landscape of FDA-cleared AI imaging tools (over 100), noting only one is cleared for pediatric use, and proposing recommendations for adequate pediatric development and validation of AI tools.
34319165.headline_result: Only 1 of >100 FDA-cleared imaging AI tools is cleared for pediatric use

34405049.clinical_problem: detecting pediatric epilepsy from resting-state functional MRI
34405049.patient_population: 63 patients with epilepsy and 259 healthy controls undergoing preoperative rs-fMRI
34405049.model_description: Machine learning classifiers (XGBoost, SVM, random forest) take PCA-derived features of resting-state fMRI latency z-score maps as input and classify subjects as epilepsy vs. healthy control.
34405049.headline_result: Best model (XGBoost): test AUC 0.79, accuracy 74%, specificity 73%, sensitivity 77%

34470531.clinical_problem: screening for congenital anomalies of the fetal heart and lungs on ultrasound
34470531.patient_population: fetal ultrasound images (sample size not stated in abstract)
34470531.model_description: A multi-scale U-Net-style model with skip connections and additive attention gates takes fetal ultrasound images as input and simultaneously segments fetal heart and lung regions.
34470531.headline_result: Outperformed existing deep-learning segmentation methods (no single metric quoted in abstract)

34566556.clinical_problem: imputing missing longitudinal MRI scans in infants to complete developmental trajectory studies
34566556.patient_population: infants in the first year of life with longitudinal MRI (sample size not stated)
34566556.model_description: A 3D multi-contrast perceptual adversarial network (MPGAN) takes an infant's T1w/T2w MRI at one time point as input and predicts/imputes the structural MRI appearance at a different developmental time point using voxel-wise and perceptual losses.
34566556.headline_result: Imputed images improved downstream regression and classification task performance (no single accuracy figure reported)

34566613.clinical_problem: classifying developmental dyslexia from functional MRI and visualizing the brain regions driving classification
34566613.patient_population: children diagnosed with developmental dyslexia and typical readers (sample size not stated)
34566613.model_description: A convolutional neural network classifies subjects as dyslexic or typical readers from functional brain imaging features, with network-visualization techniques used to generate interpretable maps of discriminative brain regions.
34566613.study_design: retrospective classification study with model-interpretability analysis

34736625.clinical_problem: using muscle imaging (pattern recognition and quantification) to diagnose pediatric neuromuscular disease
34736625.patient_population: children with neuromuscular disorders (review, no single cohort)
34736625.model_description: A historical review of two decades of pediatric muscle imaging, describing progression from qualitative pattern recognition of MRI/ultrasound 'MRI fingerprints' toward quantification and machine learning approaches for etiological diagnosis.

34755674.clinical_problem: differentiating retroperitoneal neuroblastoma from ganglioneuroblastoma in children on CT
34755674.patient_population: 172 children with neuroblastoma and 48 with ganglioneuroblastoma
34755674.model_description: CT radiomics features are extracted from non-enhanced and post-enhanced images and combined in a multivariate regression model to output the probability of neuroblastoma vs. ganglioneuroblastoma.
34755674.study_design: retrospective radiomics model-development study with training/testing split

34850259.clinical_problem: triaging radiographs to detect and classify esophageal button-battery vs. coin foreign bodies in children
34850259.patient_population: training set of 57 radiographs; test set of 103 radiographs with a foreign body and 103 without
34850259.model_description: An object detector locates esophageal foreign bodies on radiographs, and an image classifier then classifies the detected object as a button battery or coin.
34850259.headline_result: Detector 100% sensitive/specific; classifier 100% button batteries and 97.9% coins correctly classified

34939745.clinical_problem: identifying epilepsy in children from diffusion kurtosis imaging of the hippocampus
34939745.patient_population: 59 children with hippocampal epilepsy and 70 age/sex-matched controls
34939745.model_description: An SVM classifier takes hippocampal kurtosis-tensor features derived from diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI) as input and classifies subjects as epilepsy vs. normal control.

35967125.clinical_problem: segmenting white matter, gray matter and CSF on neonatal brain MRI acquired at different sites/scanners
35967125.patient_population: neonatal brain MRI from multiple sites, including a grand-challenge segmentation dataset (sample size not stated)
35967125.model_description: A CycleGAN harmonizes cross-site/cross-scanner neonatal brain MR images into the training-image domain (also reducing motion artifacts), after which a densely-connected U-Net segments white matter, gray matter and CSF.
35967125.headline_result: Better segmentation performance than existing methods on cross-site data and a grand-challenge dataset (no single metric reported in abstract)

30680611.exclusion_reason: adult-only study (community-dwelling older adults, mean age 72); not pediatric

31538277.clinical_problem: classifying conduct disorder in adolescents from structural brain MRI
31538277.patient_population: 60 adolescents with conduct disorder and 60 age/sex-matched healthy controls, all male
31538277.model_description: A 3D AlexNet CNN takes structural MRI as input and classifies adolescents as having conduct disorder vs. healthy, with saliency maps highlighting discriminative brain regions.
31538277.study_design: retrospective case-control classification study with 5-fold cross-validation

32086190.clinical_problem: predicting whether post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus in premature neonates will require intervention, from cranial ultrasound
32086190.patient_population: premature neonates with post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus (sample size not stated)
32086190.model_description: A deep-learning method (CNN incorporated into a probabilistic-atlas-based loss) segments lateral ventricles on cranial ultrasound to derive ventricular morphological phenotypes, which an SVM classifier then uses with clinical data to predict need for hydrocephalus intervention.

32337647.clinical_problem: automatically detecting scoliosis treatment (brace or implant) present on frontal radiographs
32337647.patient_population: 796 frontal radiographs of adolescents (84 brace, 325 implant, 387 no treatment), augmented to 2096 images
32337647.model_description: A CNN followed by discriminant analysis takes postero-anterior spine radiographs as input and outputs a probability of the image containing a brace, spinal implant, or no treatment.
32337647.headline_result: 98.3% of radiographs correctly classified (2.0% unclassified); 99.7% of brace radiographs correctly detected
32337647.study_design: retrospective model-development study with stratified 10-fold cross-validation

32683551.clinical_problem: predicting neurodevelopmental outcome at 12 months in very preterm infants from MR spectroscopy and diffusion tensor imaging
32683551.patient_population: 300 very preterm infants (<32 weeks) scanned at term-equivalent age; 103-115 included after exclusions
32683551.model_description: Feed-forward neural networks take selected cerebral 1H-MR-spectroscopy metabolite ratios and diffusion tensor imaging metrics from six brain regions as input and predict motor and cognitive developmental delay at 12 months corrected age.
32683551.dataset_size: 103 infants (cognitive), 115 infants (motor) after exclusions from 300 enrolled
32683551.headline_result: Cognitive delay: sensitivity 85.7%, specificity 100%; motor delay: sensitivity 76.9%, specificity 98.9%
32683551.study_design: prospective cohort study with model development

32748530.clinical_problem: establishing bone-age reference standards for Taiwanese children using automated software
32748530.model_description: BoneXpert automated software takes hand and wrist radiographs as input and outputs Greulich-Pyle and Tanner-Whitehouse 3 bone-age estimates, compared against chronological age.
32748530.release_evidence: BoneXpert version 2.5.4.1 automated software, a named commercial product
32748530.headline_result: GP and TW3 bone age deviated from chronological age by varying amounts across age/sex subgroups (reference tables established, no single summary statistic)

32927234.exclusion_reason: conventional fMRI activation/behavioral analysis; no machine learning or AI component described

32955457.body_region: radius, distal tibia, proximal tibia, distal femur, calcaneus
32955457.clinical_problem: estimating chronological age from bone-age-assessment stage and non-radiological factors in young individuals, for legal/clinical age determination
32955457.model_description: Machine learning models take MRI-based bone-development staging (radiologist-assessed) plus weight, height and questionnaire data (Tanner scale, activity level, origin, residence) as input and output an estimated chronological age or minor/adult classification.
32955457.headline_result: Minor vs. adult classification accuracy 0.90 (male), 0.84 (female); CA estimation MAE 0.95 y (male), 1.24 y (female)

33018319.clinical_problem: automated early detection of juvenile myoclonic epilepsy from diffusion MRI
33018319.model_description: CNN-based transfer learning models (Inception_v3, Inception_v4, Inception_resnet_v2) take connectivity matrices derived from HARDI and NODDI diffusion MRI as input and classify subjects as JME vs. normal.

33048183.clinical_problem: classifying severity of liver stiffness (chronic liver disease) in children and young adults without MR elastography
33048183.patient_population: 273 subjects with known or suspected chronic liver disease (178 internal cross-validation, 95 external validation)
33048183.model_description: DeepLiverNet, a deep transfer learning model, takes T2-weighted MRI images plus clinical/demographic data as input and classifies liver stiffness as no/mild vs. moderate/severe, referenced against MR elastography.
33048183.headline_result: Internal AuROC 0.86, accuracy 88.0%; external validation AuROC 0.79, accuracy 80.0%
33048183.study_design: retrospective model development with internal cross-validation and external validation

33058279.clinical_problem: reducing motion-related bias in diffusion MRI parameter estimation, tested in part on a pediatric ADHD dataset
33058279.patient_population: individual- and group-level diffusion MRI data, including a dataset of children with ADHD
33058279.model_description: A hierarchical convolutional neural network estimates diffusion kurtosis/tensor parameters from motion-corrupted diffusion MRI after data rejection, aiming to minimize residual motion-level-dependent bias compared with conventional correction methods.
33058279.headline_result: H-CNN minimally sensitive to motion effects even with 70-90% of data rejected; ameliorated spurious group differences in a pediatric ADHD dataset

33190515.exclusion_reason: model predicts body composition from anthropometric/demographic (non-imaging) data; DXA imaging used only as reference standard, not as model input; mixed adult and child population without pediatric-specific analysis

27741066.exclusion_reason: predicts emergency department return visits from clinical/administrative data; no imaging component

31681458.clinical_problem: parcellating the cortical surface of neonatal brain MRI into anatomically meaningful regions
31681458.model_description: Spherical convolution, pooling and upsampling operations extend CNNs (U-Net and SegNet architectures) to spherical cortical surface meshes, taking neonatal cortical surface data as input and outputting a parcellation into anatomical regions.
31681458.headline_result: Outperformed spherical SegNet and a prior patch-wise classification method (no single number reported in abstract)

30029804.exclusion_reason: fMRI functional-connectivity analysis of language networks in infants; machine learning mentioned only as an inspirational analogy, not used as a method

30237302.exclusion_reason: commentary on neuroradiology common data elements and standardized reporting, not pediatric-specific and not primarily about an AI imaging model; machine learning mentioned only in passing

30374323.exclusion_reason: resting-state fMRI graph-theory analysis of infant emotional behavior; no machine learning/AI method used

30440540.clinical_problem: automatically identifying complete atrioventricular activity cycles in fetal Doppler echocardiography for antenatal cardiac assessment
30440540.patient_population: 5 pregnant women (21st-27th gestational week), 20 records of 10 seconds each
30440540.model_description: A neural network takes a pair of 1D signals representing the pulse-wave Doppler envelope extracted from fetal echocardiography video as input and identifies epochs containing a complete, readable cardiac cycle.
30440540.dataset_size: 20 records (10 s each) from 5 pregnant women

28843999.clinical_problem: predicting inattention and impulsivity symptom severity in ADHD from resting-state fMRI connectivity
28843999.patient_population: 74 boys with ADHD and 69 age-matched controls (ADHD-200 Consortium)
28843999.model_description: A LASSO-based predictive model takes intra- and inter-network temporal connectivity features (sample entropy, phase synchronization) from resting-state fMRI as input and predicts continuous inattention and impulsivity symptom scores.
28843999.headline_result: Prediction performance r=0.79 (inattention), r=0.48 (impulsivity), both p<10^-8
28843999.study_design: retrospective predictive-modeling study using a public multi-site cohort (ADHD-200)

28902466.model_family: random forest regression with auto-context model
28902466.clinical_problem: deformable registration of infant brain MRI acquired at different developmental time points for early brain development studies
28902466.patient_population: infants scanned longitudinally at 2 weeks, 3, 6, 9 and 12 months
28902466.model_description: A multioutput random forest regression with an auto-context model learns the evolution of anatomical shape and appearance from longitudinal infant MRI, then predicts deformation fields and appearance changes to register images from two different developmental time points.
28902466.headline_result: Higher registration accuracy than nonlearning-based registration methods (no single number reported in abstract)

27680743.exclusion_reason: animal model study (spontaneously hypertensive rats), not a human pediatric study

28268406.clinical_problem: automatically recognizing the fetal facial standard plane on prenatal ultrasound
28268406.patient_population: fetal ultrasound images (sample size not stated in abstract)
28268406.model_description: A very deep convolutional network with small (3x3) filters takes ultrasound images as input and recognizes the fetal facial standard plane (axial, coronal, sagittal).
28268406.headline_result: State-of-the-art recognition results, superior to previous methods (no single number reported in abstract)

23947815.exclusion_reason: gene-expression/microarray molecular profiling study; genomics without imaging

16703344.clinical_problem: distinguishing brain metabolite differences in adolescents with very low birth weight or small-for-gestational-age from controls
16703344.patient_population: 54 adolescents (very low birth weight, small-for-gestational-age at term, and controls)
16703344.model_description: A probabilistic neural network takes chemical-shift regions (NAA, choline, creatine peaks) from proton MR spectroscopy as input and classifies adolescents into birth-history subgroups.
16703344.headline_result: Correct classification of 52/54 adolescents, sensitivity and specificity >93% for all groups

16189473.exclusion_reason: standard task-based fMRI activation analysis in children; no machine learning or AI method used

38805609.exclusion_reason: prediction model uses only clinical/demographic characteristics from the first prenatal visit; no imaging input

39788362.clinical_problem: identifying patterns of twin fetal growth discordance from serial ultrasound and Doppler assessments, and their association with adverse perinatal outcomes
39788362.patient_population: 823 twin pregnancies (647 dichorionic, 176 monochorionic) with at least 3 ultrasound assessments after 18 weeks
39788362.model_description: K-means clustering, an unsupervised machine learning algorithm, groups longitudinal intertwin growth and Doppler discordance measurements (from serial ultrasound biometry/Doppler) into distinct trajectory patterns, which are then tested for association with a composite adverse perinatal outcome.
39788362.headline_result: Best predictive model AUC 0.802 (95% CI 0.712-0.892), combining discordance trajectory and cerebroplacental ratio discordance
39788362.study_design: retrospective longitudinal cohort study with unsupervised clustering

39870000.clinical_problem: predicting sex and age from diffusion MRI tractography, with interpretable identification of contributing white matter tracts
39870000.patient_population: children (n=9,345) and young adults (n=1,065) from large diffusion MRI datasets
39870000.model_description: TractGraphFormer combines a graph CNN (capturing local white-matter geometry/connectivity) with a transformer (global self-attention) to take diffusion MRI tractography as input and predict subject sex and age, with an attention module highlighting predictive tracts.
39870000.headline_result: Strong performance for sex and age prediction with consistent predictive anatomical tracts across two datasets (no single accuracy figure given)
39870000.study_design: retrospective method-development study across two large cohorts

39898398.clinical_problem: shortening pediatric brain MRI acquisition time while maintaining image quality
39898398.patient_population: 46 pediatric patients undergoing 3D T1-weighted brain MRI
39898398.model_description: A deep-learning-based reconstruction algorithm is applied to accelerated 3D T1-weighted pediatric brain MRI acquisitions, taking undersampled k-space/image data as input and outputting reconstructed images compared with conventional and non-DL accelerated reconstructions.
39898398.release_evidence: vendor deep-learning reconstruction algorithm used on a clinical 3T scanner (GE HealthCare SIGNA Premier)
39898398.headline_result: Scan time reduced 29.3-40.7%; DL reconstruction improved aSNR, aCNR and overall image quality vs. conventional acquisition (all P<0.05)

39946338.clinical_problem: using AI and 4D ultrasound to analyze fetal facial expressions as a potential prenatal marker of neurodevelopmental disorders
39946338.model_description: A narrative review of AI-assisted analysis of 4D ultrasound fetal facial movements, discussing their potential as diagnostic markers for prenatal neurodevelopmental disorders such as Bell's Palsy and Ramsay Hunt Syndrome.

40195943.clinical_problem: using AI-enhanced 4D ultrasound to detect fetal anomalies, neurodevelopmental markers and congenital heart defects, linking fetal programming to adult disease risk
40195943.model_description: A narrative review synthesizing AI-enhanced 4D ultrasound applications for detecting fetal anomalies, neurodevelopmental markers and congenital heart defects, and discussing links to Barker's Hypothesis of fetal origins of adult disease.

40460372.clinical_problem: relating upper airway volume (sleep-disordered breathing) to brain structure and cognition in children
40460372.patient_population: 11,875 children from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study, ages 9-10 at baseline, followed 5 years
40460372.model_description: A deep learning model is applied to over 5.5 million brain MRI slices to automatically segment and derive upper airway volume, which is then related to cognition scores and cortical gray matter volumes.
40460372.headline_result: Habitual snorers had 1.2 cm³ smaller airway volume (P<0.001); larger airway volume predicted higher Total Cognition Composite score (+3.68 points per log-unit, P<0.001)
40460372.study_design: retrospective analysis of a large multi-site prospective cohort (ABCD)

40507258.clinical_problem: clarifying segmentation performance metrics discussed in a prior review of AI for neuroimaging in pediatric cancer
40507258.model_description: A brief author reply to a reader comment on a prior review, 'Artificial Intelligence for Neuroimaging in Pediatric Cancer,' discussing segmentation performance metrics; contains no new model or data.

40507618.clinical_problem: reviewing AI's role in predicting and improving adverse pregnancy outcomes, including via ultrasound and continuous monitoring
40507618.patient_population: pregnant women (scoping review of 5 included studies, 2020-2024)
40507618.model_description: A scoping review of 5 studies applying machine learning (e.g., XGBoost, random forest) to predict adverse pregnancy outcomes such as preterm birth, hypertensive disorders and gestational diabetes, discussing ultrasound-based and monitoring applications and ethical issues.

40772171.exclusion_reason: systematic review of the Bishop score for predicting successful labor induction; machine learning/AI mentioned only briefly in passing, not the focus

41276667.clinical_problem: detecting and lateralizing pediatric airway foreign body aspiration from clinical data and chest radiographs
41276667.patient_population: 58 pediatric patients evaluated for suspected airway foreign body aspiration (2015-2024)
41276667.model_description: GPT-4.1, a vision-enabled multimodal large language model, takes structured clinical data and chest radiographs as input and classifies cases as right-bronchus, left-bronchus, or no aspiration, benchmarked against bronchoscopy.
41276667.release_evidence: GPT-4.1 is a named commercially available large language model
41276667.headline_result: Overall accuracy 62.3%, precision 23.3%, recall 19.0%, F1 0.21; detected only 4/12 confirmed aspirations and missed all left-bronchus cases

38220469.clinical_problem: characterizing brain connectome abnormalities in youth at familial risk for bipolar disorder using task-based fMRI
38220469.patient_population: 119 depressed/anxious youth at familial risk for bipolar disorder (age 14.9±1.6) and 57 typically developing controls (age 14.8±1.7)
38220469.model_description: Generalized psychophysiological interaction analysis derives task-based fMRI connectome patterns, and machine learning of topological network metrics is used to classify high-risk youth vs. controls.

38389213.exclusion_reason: gut microbiota (16S rRNA sequencing) study of bone density in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis; non-imaging, microbiome-based

38472163.clinical_problem: reviewing machine-learning approaches for detecting ADHD from resting-state functional MRI in school-age children
38472163.patient_population: review of studies using the ADHD-200 database and related rs-fMRI cohorts
38472163.model_description: A review of prior studies that use resting-state fMRI functional-network features with machine learning and deep learning methods (network/atlas selection, feature extraction/selection, classification) to detect ADHD.

38492045.clinical_problem: predicting event-free survival after remission induction in high-risk pediatric neuroblastoma from 123I-MIBG SPECT-CT
38492045.patient_population: 172 patients with high-risk neuroblastoma reviewed; 87 met inclusion criteria (training/validation 7:3)
38492045.model_description: Radiomics features extracted from 123I-MIBG SPECT-CT images of the lumbar vertebral bodies are combined with clinical risk factors in a Cox-regression nomogram to predict event-free survival after remission induction.
38492045.study_design: retrospective radiomics-nomogram development and validation study

38509226.exclusion_reason: infant fecal metabolomics (NMR spectroscopy of stool) related to social behavior; non-radiologic, non-imaging

38755982.exclusion_reason: dental panoramic radiograph segmentation of impacted teeth; dental imaging excluded per protocol

38759068.clinical_problem: differentiating ventricular septal defect from tetralogy of Fallot on fetal echocardiography
38759068.patient_population: 105 fetal echocardiography images of tetralogy of Fallot and 96 of ventricular septal defect
38759068.model_description: Four CNN architectures (VGG19, ResNet50, NTS-Net, WSDAN) classify fetal echocardiography images as tetralogy of Fallot vs. ventricular septal defect, compared by sensitivity, specificity and AUC.

38786561.model_family: explainable AI / machine learning decision-support system
38786561.clinical_problem: predicting dystocic (obstructed) labor and mode of delivery from intrapartum ultrasound measurements of fetal head position
38786561.patient_population: pregnant women in labor undergoing vaginal digital exam and intrapartum ultrasound (sample size not stated)
38786561.model_description: AIDA, a human-in-the-loop explainable AI algorithm, takes four ultrasound-measured 'geometric parameters' of fetal head position/engagement as input and classifies labor progress into five reference classes predicting delivery outcome (spontaneous vaginal, operative vaginal, or cesarean).

38872945.clinical_problem: automatic cortical surface parcellation of the fetal brain to study neurodevelopmental trajectories
